r11: Is the delivered image itself clearly a screenshot/interface, a flat poster, advertisement, illustrated cover, page, chart, illustration or painting reproduction, or an obvious computer render? Answer YES even if the graphic contains a photograph. Answer NO for a photo of an actual object or scene with meaningful physical context, including packaging, signs, screens and artworks. A visible hand, table, environment or object thickness can establish context; when unsure answer NO.
r12: Identify the medium of the whole frame. YES means the image itself is a screenshot, flat artwork or illustration, advertisement, poster, magazine cover, document, chart, or obvious 3D render. A reproduction remains excluded when it contains a photograph or text. NO means a camera photograph of a real object or scene, including a product or physical screen with surroundings or depth. If the visual evidence is ambiguous, answer NO.
r13: Exclude YES for an interface screenshot or flat graphic reproduction: a poster, advertisement, page, cover, chart, drawing, painting or obvious synthetic render. A flat composition with text laid over a photographic image is still a graphic. Keep NO for real photographs of packages, signs, screens, printed artwork or sculpture if a hand, physical edge, perspective or surroundings show an object in a scene. Keep uncertain cases.
r14: Is this entire image itself a screenshot, an obvious computer-rendered scene, a diagram, chart, illustration, painting reproduction, poster, page or graphic advertisement? Answer YES. Does the image show a physically photographed package, object, sign, screen or artwork with visible surroundings, hand or depth? Answer NO. Text, blur, imperfect sharpness and visual attractiveness alone never establish exclusion. If uncertain answer NO.
r15: Decide whether the input is a photographic scene, not whether it is good. Exclude YES for screenshots or visible software controls; flat text-and-image posters or covers; near-frame-filling pages, charts, drawings and paintings; and unmistakable computer renders. A photograph displayed inside a design does not make it a photograph. Keep NO for real objects in a photographed scene, even if covered in print, and for uncertain cases.
r16: Does the entire input present a non-photographic medium: screenshot or user interface; poster, printed page, drawing or painting reproduced as the image; graph or obvious synthetic render? Answer YES. Answer NO if the camera captured a physical object or environment with meaningful physical depth or surrounding context. Printed packaging and artwork in a scene are still objects; an image embedded in a screenshot or poster does not change its medium. If uncertain answer NO.
r17: Exclude clearly non-photographic inputs: screenshots, games or app interfaces; flat advertisements, posters, magazine covers or pages; drawings, paintings or charts; and obvious computer renders. Look for hand, tabletop, room, object boundary or perspective indicating that the input is instead a photograph of physical print, artwork, packaging or screen; keep such photos eligible. When the medium is genuinely uncertain keep it eligible. Is the input excluded? YES or NO.
r18: Determine the source of the whole frame. A screenshot or digital interface, an illustration, a painting reproduction, an advertisement or poster, a full-frame document or chart, or an obvious render is excluded YES. A real photo with a hand, table, environment or physical object geometry is eligible NO, even if it contains a page or image. The existence of lettering alone does not make a physical scene a flat design. Answer NO if not clear.
r19: Is the image itself a flat graphic, a screenshot or UI, or an obvious computer-generated render? Examples of flat graphics include poster designs, covers with photographs and headlines, advertisements, document reproductions, illustrations, paintings and charts. YES excludes these. Physical photographed scenes or objects, such as a book held over a table, are NO even when they have printed text and art. If uncertain, NO.
r20: Check the frame before rating. Exclude YES if the delivered image is itself a screenshot/interface, near-full-frame poster, advertisement, cover, page, diagram, chart, illustration or painting reproduction, or an obvious render. Keep NO when it photographs a physical object or scene with meaningful context, even if that object displays text, a picture, artwork or a screen. Poor photographic quality is not grounds for exclusion. When uncertain say NO.
